input: This case sets out the pricing position for a contract cleaning service. The price is $292 per unit and the variable cost is $202 per unit, which means that each unit contributes $90 towards the fixed costs of $126k per year. Break-even volume for the service is 1400 units per year, against a current volume of 5292 units per year, and the volume figures are last year's actuals. At the current price, then, the service operates well above break-even: volume could fall by more than half before the contribution ceased to cover the fixed costs, although a fall of that size would leave no margin for the costs that the case does not itemise. It is important to note that the case does not estimate the effect of the price on volume, and that omission bounds what the figures can show. A higher price raises the contribution per unit and lowers the break-even volume on paper, but if the higher price costs volume, the service can move towards break-even while the arithmetic moves the other way. The figures therefore support a statement about the present position only: at last year's volume and the present price, the service covers its fixed costs with room to spare, and any repricing decision would need a volume response that this case does not provide.
